hints: Focus on what the p-orbital description tells you about electron count, remember each orbital holds a maximum of two electrons.
Element Y has three p-orbitals occupied with only one paired, so count up its p-electrons to find it is oxygen in Period 2.
Element Z has only two p-orbitals occupied in Period 3, work out which element that fits and then pair it with oxygen to make a stable compound.
walkthrough:
**Decode Element Y in Period 2**

Think of the three p-orbitals as three boxes. All three have something in them, but only one box is full.

That means: 1 full orbital (2 electrons) + 2 half-filled orbitals (1 + 1 electrons) = 4 p-electrons.

So the configuration ends in $2p^4$:
$$1s^2 2s^2 2p^4$$
This is oxygen, $\text{O}$.

**Decode Element Z in Period 3**

Now only two of the three p-boxes are occupied. That means only 2 p-electrons, each singly occupying a different orbital.

So the configuration ends in $3p^2$:
$$1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^2$$
This is silicon, $\text{Si}$.

**Combine Y and Z into Compound X**

We have silicon and oxygen. Silicon is in Group 14 and needs 4 more electrons, oxygen is in Group 16 and needs 2 more electrons.

One Si therefore combines with two O atoms to balance valencies, giving silicon dioxide:
$$\text{Si} + 2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{SiO}_2$$

options.A: Incorrect. $\text{CCl}_4$ needs carbon and chlorine. Carbon is $2p^2$ (only two p-orbitals occupied) and chlorine is $3p^5$ (all three p-orbitals occupied), so neither matches the descriptions.
options.B: Incorrect. $\text{SiCl}_4$ correctly contains Si for element Z, but chlorine is $1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^5$ with all three p-orbitals occupied. Element Y must be oxygen, not chlorine.
options.C: Correct. Element Y is oxygen ($2p^4$, three orbitals occupied, one fully occupied) and element Z is silicon ($3p^2$, only two orbitals occupied). Together they form the stable compound $\text{SiO}_2$.
options.D: Incorrect. $\text{SO}_2$ correctly contains O for element Y, but sulfur is $3p^4$ with all three p-orbitals occupied (one full, two half-filled). Element Z must have only two p-orbitals occupied, which is silicon, not sulfur.
